findings.title: payment-application-generator forges unapproved CO and uncapped SOV progress into G702 payment due
findings.description: add_change_order() is documented as adding an 'approved' change order but performs no approval, status, or auth check — any caller can inflate change_orders_total and invent SOV lines. create_application() then accepts arbitrary progress['work']/['materials'] with no clamp to scheduled_value. calculate_payment_due()/generate_g702() emit current_payment_due from those forged totals. Distinct from the already-reported negative retainage_percent bug on the same skill.
findings.impact: A contractor (or anyone invoking the generator) can mint a multi-million-dollar payment application: PoC forges a $2M CO onto a $1M contract and bills $5M completed → $4.5M current payment due at 10% retainage, producing fraudulent AIA G702/G703 documents.
findings.attack_path:
1. Caller constructs PaymentApplicationGenerator(original_contract=1_000_000).
2. setup_sov with a real $500k line.
3. add_change_order(2_000_000, 'Phantom CO') with no approval workflow — contract sum becomes $3M and SOV gains CO-01.
4. create_application(..., progress={'001':{'work':3_000_000},'CO-01':{'work':2_000_000}}) with no SOV cap.
5. calculate_payment_due / generate_g702 report current_payment_due=$4,500,000.
findings.remediation: Require an approved CO id/status before mutating change_orders_total; clamp period progress so cumulative completed ≤ scheduled_value; reject non-positive amounts; require a separate approver role before generate_g702/export.

findings.title: cash-flow-forecaster negative retention_percent permanently inflates inflows/outflows
findings.description: _generate_item_payments computes net_amount = total_amount * (1 - retention_percent) with no bounds check, then only posts a retention release when retention_percent > 0. A negative retention therefore scales every period payment up and skips the offsetting release, so lifetime scheduled cash permanently exceeds the item total.
findings.impact: Financing and owner-draw forecasts can be inflated 50–100%+ (PoC: $1M revenue with retention=-0.50 yields $1.5M total inflow and no retention release). Cost items with negative retention similarly invent outflows for vendor cash planning.
findings.attack_path:
1. Caller adds a revenue (or cost) item via add_revenue_item/add_cost_item with retention=-0.50.
2. generate_payment_schedule → _generate_item_payments sets net_amount = total * 1.5 and distributes it.
3. Because retention_percent > 0 is false, no retention release payment is created.
4. generate_cash_flow_forecast / get_funding_requirements trust the inflated schedule.
findings.remediation: Clamp retention_percent to [0, 1]; reject negatives; always reconcile period nets + release to equal total_amount; validate on add_cost_item/add_revenue_item.

findings.title: curated budget-variance-analyzer revise_budget hides overruns; use_contingency unbounded
findings.description: revise_budget() overwrites revised_budget and forecast with any caller-supplied value and no approval, audit gate, or comparison to actuals — turning a -$150k overrun into a +$50k 'under budget' variance. use_contingency() increments contingency_used by any amount (including millions) with no contingency pool, remaining-balance check, or approval, and adds that amount onto the target code's revised_budget. Distinct from the already-reported toolkit adjust_budget finding (different API/path).
findings.impact: Cost controllers or anyone calling the analyzer can erase visible overruns from variance reports and invent unlimited contingency transfers, falsifying EAC/VAC and executive cost-control dashboards.
findings.attack_path:
1. Cost code 03 has original budget $200k and actual $350k (variance -$150k).
2. Attacker calls revise_budget('03', 400_000) with no approval → variance becomes +$50k.
3. Attacker calls use_contingency(5_000_000, '03') with no remaining-contingency check → revised_budget becomes $5.4M and contingency_used=$5M.
4. generate_variance_report reflects the forged healthy status.
findings.remediation: Require dual-control approval for revise_budget; cap revised_budget changes; initialize a contingency pool and reject use_contingency when amount <= 0 or amount > remaining; audit both mutations.

findings.title: bim-cost-estimation-cwicr project_name path traversal writes Excel outside output_path
findings.description: generate_estimate_report builds excel_path via f-string concatenation f"{output_path}/{project_name}_Estimate.xlsx" with no sanitization of project_name. estimate_from_bim_model sets project_name = Path(model_path).stem, and callers can also pass project_name directly. A project_name containing ../ escapes the intended output directory and writes the estimate workbook elsewhere.
findings.impact: Attacker-controlled project_name (or a model_path stem crafted with path separators where accepted) overwrites or plants Excel files outside the designated estimates folder — integrity/availability impact on adjacent project data.
findings.attack_path:
1. Caller invokes generate_estimate_report(..., project_name='../outside/pwned', output_path='/data/estimates').
2. excel_path resolves to /data/outside/pwned_Estimate.xlsx (outside /data/estimates).
3. pd.ExcelWriter creates/overwrites that path.
4. PoC confirmed Path.resolve() escape and write into a sibling directory.
findings.remediation: Use Path(output_path) / f"{safe_name}_Estimate.xlsx" after stripping separators from project_name; resolve and assert the final path is contained under output_path.resolve(); reject names with .. or path separators.
